thread:
andrea: Heads up — I hit a weird regression with async tool_call + structured output in the py-sdk while building the sample app. The dataclass I return from the tool is coming back as a plain dict when awaited.

andrea: Minimal repro:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient, ToolResult
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Item:
    id: int
    name: str

async def my_tool(args) -> Item:
    return Item(id=1, name="x")

client = AsyncClient()
resp = await client.call_tool_async("my_tool", args={})
# resp.output is a dict, not Item
```

andrea: This used to coerce to Item (dataclass) in the sync path. Async path returns dict. Anyone else seen this?

sam: I remember a related change around the async deserialization refactor. Might be missing the coercion step after streaming/await path. Can you paste a small repr of the actual payload you got?

andrea: Sure — the response body from the RPC looks correct: `{"type":"tool_result","output":{"id":1,"name":"x"}}` but SDK gives me `{'id': 1, 'name': 'x'}` instead of Item.

tyler: Repro'd locally. Sync client: returns Item. Async client: returns dict. Suspect the place where we call _deserialize_and_coerce() isn't awaited or runs on a different codepath for streaming result completion.

olivia: Also seeing sporadic failures when retry kicks in — sometimes the tool gets invoked twice and we end up with a list of outputs; SDK then normalizes to list and loses type info. Might be related.

andrea: For the sample app onboarding this is confusing to users — tutorial shows dataclass->object roundtrip and it breaks only in async.

sam: Created an issue and linked a tiny failing test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/432 (WIP). Adding @tyler to triage.

tyler: I'll take it. Quick patch idea: ensure the async result finalization pipeline calls the same postprocessing hooks as sync. Also add explicit unit test for dataclass coercion on both clients.

olivia: Small UX ask — can we add a short note in sample-apps/python/README about how dataclass coercion works with streaming vs non-streaming calls? Saves confusion while we fix.

andrea: Agreed. I've already dropped a PR with README tweak: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/210 (WIP).

ci-bot: build/pytest — MyPy and tests run queued for branch: fix/async-dataclass-coerce (expected ~12m)

sam: Action items: 1) tyler to open PR for async pipeline fix; 2) andrea to add failing test case to sdk test suite; 3) olivia to add README note in sample apps.

andrea: One more oddity — type annotations on the tool signature (-> Item) seem ignored unless you pass `return_type=Item` explicitly. Probably fine to document but we should try to preserve annotation where available.

tyler: Good call. I'll check the annotation introspection code path. If it's flaky for async we should fall back to explicit `return_type` but emit a warning.

olivia: :thumbsup: Looks like a small but important DX gap.

andrea: Thanks all — assigning the linked issue to tyler, dropping the failing snippet into tests, and will update the sample app README. If anyone finds extra edge cases (nested dataclasses, optional fields), drop them in the GH issue comments.

sam: Marking this as P1 for the SDK parity tracker.

tyler: I'll push a draft PR today and ping here when CI passes.

andrea: Awesome — appreciate the quick turnaround.
